narrative:
The model has predicted that you have a 52% chance of failing your final year, which means there is a significant likelihood that you may not meet the necessary requirements to pass. As a result, you are required to take remedial courses to help improve your understanding and performance in your studies.

Several factors contributed to this prediction. One of the most influential aspects is your desire for higher education, which, while commendable, may indicate that you are feeling pressure to perform well. However, your history of past failures—having one previous class failure—also weighs heavily against you, as it suggests that you may struggle with certain subjects. Additionally, the reason you chose your school, which is based on its proximity to home, may not provide the same level of academic challenge or support that other students experience.

These factors collectively push the prediction toward the possibility of failing. Your family size is smaller than average, and while you do receive family support, you are not currently receiving extra educational assistance or participating in additional classes, which could help bolster your academic performance. 

Moving forward, it is essential to engage actively in the remedial courses. These classes are designed to address the gaps in your knowledge and provide you with the tools you need to succeed. Additionally, consider seeking extra help from teachers or tutors, and explore ways to enhance your study habits and time management skills. Taking these steps can significantly improve your chances of passing and achieving your educational goals.
